questions.question: What starts the workflow, and which starting events should it ignore?
questions.why: The trigger controls where the workflow runs.

questions.question: What should exist or change when it finishes?
questions.why: A visible result is easier to test.

questions.question: At what point do you want the workflow to ask or stop?
questions.why: Some actions need a person to confirm them.

exit_criteria: Identify the trigger, finished result and a condition that should stop the workflow.

questions.question: Which accounts and apps does the workflow touch?
questions.why: Each connection needs a clear owner.

questions.question: What is the least access each connection needs?
questions.why: The workflow should have enough access for its job.

questions.question: Who can replace a connection when access expires?
questions.why: Automation should have a named recovery path.

exit_criteria: Give each connected service an owner, minimum access and safe credential storage.

questions.question: Can you walk from one example input to its final output?
questions.why: A real example exposes branching conditions.

questions.question: What should happen when the same event arrives twice?
questions.why: Retries and duplicate events should not double the result.

questions.question: Who needs an alert if only part of the workflow succeeded?
questions.why: Partial work should be visible and recoverable.

questions.question: Will an AI make any decision in this workflow, and when should a person take over?
questions.why: Automatic decisions need an agreed limit and a fallback.

exit_criteria: Record retries, duplicate prevention and alerts for failure.

questions.question: Which sample inputs can be tested without contacting real customers?
questions.why: The team can verify the flow safely.

questions.question: Which step should we replay to prove that a retry is safe?
Who checks the first real run after the test passes?
questions.why: Someone needs to notice a problem early.

exit_criteria: Cover success, duplicate, failure and no-action cases with safe samples.
